# Card 226: task-force declaration proposal (objection window 226-taskforce)

Category: task-force declaration. Proposed by: product manager (ready), Claude seat, ctx-1 of card 226.
Probe reference: .mob/records/probes/2026-10-30.jsonl (probe taken 2026-10-31T01:20 UTC; codex 01:20:30, copilot 01:20:36, grok 01:20:37, agy 01:20:40). The probe goes stale at 02:20 UTC (60 minutes, probe_is_stale): any seat or poll that starts at or after that time re-probes first.
Repositories: the card, its record and its window are in phrase-lang (C:\Users\ringe\projects\phrase-lang); the code the card changes is in mob-defaults (C:\Users\ringe\mob-crosscli: decider.py and its tests, reusing facilitator.py and mob_process.py). Every command names its working directory.
Start: card 226 is the corrective card for MD-002 (open FAIL) and audit flag F-070 (audits 56 and 57); it starts as the corrective card the gate asks for, so no waiver is needed.

## Task force
- Product manager (ready): Claude | why: refines card 226 at ready; keeps the Done checks within D157 (three, one criterion each), names the value and metric, confirms the "Intent:" line (D165) will quote D163 and D164, and holds the "reuse card 208's rules, no second implementation" line | context: ctx-1
- Architect (slice): Claude | why: decides how decider.py reaches card 208's rules (call the same functions in mob_process.py: probe_is_stale, claude_wait_problem, rotation_reason, seat_use_line, last_seating, and the facilitator's gate_seat logic, instead of a second copy), numbers the criteria 1 to 3 before red (D157), writes the assumption line in the slice (D166, because this card changes a rule), and checks D136; the card record checker requires a slice seat | context: ctx-2
- QA engineer (red): Claude | why: turns each Done check's ZOMBIES into failing tests in the mob-defaults tests for decider.py (a stale probe, a fresh probe, a Claude voter while another model has waited longer, a never-seated model, an unreadable seat-use history, a refusal with no voter launched), one criterion per red-green cycle (D157), writes the "Intent:" line before the first red (D165), red first (D137) | context: ctx-3
- Backend developer [author] (green, refactor): Claude | why: wires decider.py to card 208's rules so each red test passes; vote parsing, the Decider protocol, sandboxed clones and the real-tree verification stay untouched; the author does not review or QA their own increment | context: ctx-4
- Independent reviewer (audit lens) [reviewer]: Claude | why: non-author review of the diff against D163 and D164 and the card's invariants (card-mode seats keep card 208's gate; no new strictness beyond D163), with a loophole lens: can a voter start on a stale probe, can a refusal still launch another voter, can the reason be typed by a seat instead of built from the probe and history, is the seat-use line written before the voter starts, does an unreadable probe result get read as "no quota" | context: ctx-5
- Delivery lead (ship): Claude | why: confirms the tests, the card record, the probe lines and that the commits cite D163 and D164 before each commit lands; stages .mob/records/seat-use.jsonl with the card as card 208 requires; the card record checker requires a ship seat with its own commit evidence | context: ctx-6
- Product manager (signoff): Claude | why: a fresh context signs off against the three Done checks, because the refinement seat may not hold the second seat | context: ctx-7

Seven seats cover the six roles the card record checker requires (ready, slice, red, green, ship, signoff) plus the independent reviewer. The reviewer seat is named "Independent reviewer (audit lens)", never "auditor": auditor_seated_problems refuses any card seat whose role contains "auditor", because the auditor is external to the mob and never seated.

## Reason for Claude seats
Probes at 01:20 UTC (.mob/records/probes/2026-10-30.jsonl) show Codex, Copilot, Grok and agy without usable quota: codex "You've hit your usage limit" (exit 1); copilot has_quota=False remaining=-5 entitlement=1500 (resets 2026-11-01); grok 402 Payment Required, usage balance exhausted; agy 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED (resets in 44h4m46s). No other model is available, so no available model has waited longer than Claude (claude_wait_problem returns nothing) and a Claude seat is allowed under D163 and D164. Each seat is a distinct fresh context (ready ctx-1, slice ctx-2, red ctx-3, green ctx-4, reviewer ctx-5, ship ctx-6, signoff ctx-7), and nobody reviews or QAs their own increment. The reason recorded for each Claude seat is the one rotation_reason builds from this probe and the seat-use history (never typed by a seat). Non-Claude models come first again as soon as a fresh probe shows quota (D163: balanced rotation, not a rule against Claude).

## Left out
UX designer and frontend developer (no user interface); database developer (no database; the seat-use history is an append-only JSONL file that card 208 already defined); security (no new trust boundary: the Decider's sandboxed clones and the real-tree verification are invariants the card does not change, and the reviewer checks them); technical writer (no document); language designer and grammar designer (no language change); performance engineer (no hot path: one probe-age check and one history read per voter); DevOps or runner expert (the card changes decider.py, not the hook, a workflow or the facilitator loop); agile coach (no process change: D157, D158, D165 and D166 are applied, not changed; the rule itself was decided in D163 and D164).

## Domain expert (refinement)
Should a member with different domain knowledge or context join now? No. The card applies card 208's existing rules to a second caller: the architect and backend developer already work in decider.py, facilitator.py and mob_process.py (cards 208 and 210 touched the same gate), and the risks specific to this card (a stale probe at voter start, rotation among models with and without quota, a Claude voter refused while another model has waited longer, a history that cannot be trusted, the reason in the decision record) are exactly the Done checks and their ZOMBIES, each pinned by a red test, with the independent reviewer (audit lens) carrying the loophole lens above. If a slice needs knowledge no seat holds, any member adds an expert through a Decider (mid-card addition, with the Decider id). Adding a seat now would add a context and a poll without a gap it fills.

## Reuse of card 208's rules (no second implementation)
Decision seats use the same functions card 208 built: probe_is_stale (60-minute limit) and re-probe, claude_wait_problem (D164 least-recently-used), rotation_reason (the recorded reason), seat_use_line and last_seating (the shared history .mob/records/seat-use.jsonl), and the facilitator's gate_seat order (re-probe if stale, read the history, refuse or append the line, then build the reason). decider.py calls them (or the one gate_seat path); it does not copy them. A second copy would let the two gates drift apart, which is how MD-002 arose. The slice (architect) decides the seam; the reviewer checks that no rule is duplicated.

## Product value and metric
Value the card returns to: MD-002 (open FAIL) closes. After card 208 the seat gate checks card-mode seats, but a Decider run (and every objection-window poll, which runs through decider.py) still seats voters with no fresh-probe check, no least-recently-used rotation and no recorded reason, so the load can pile onto one model again without anyone seeing it (the failure D163 names: defaulting to all-Claude while others have capacity). When this lands, decision seats spread the load like card seats and each decision record shows why a Claude voter was seated, so an auditor can recompute rotation from git.
Metrics that move (read from the decision records, the probe file and seat-use.jsonl in git, not self-reported by the seats):
1. Decision seats enforced by the runner like card seats: decision seats seated on a stale probe (60 minutes or older) or out of rotation (a Claude voter while another available model had waited longer), counted per Decider or window run. Today the runner checks neither, so the count is not enforced (audits 56 and 57 found it unenforced); target 0 for every run after the card lands, and a run that would breach is refused before any voter starts.
2. Claude share of decision seats while other models had capacity: the Claude voters seated on a probe that showed at least one other model available, divided by all decision seats on such probes. Target: no more than its least-recently-used turn; it is read, not capped (D164 chose least-recently-used, not a ratio cap). Companion check, not a target: decision seats with no recorded reason for a Claude voter, target 0.
Read at the first Decider or window run after the card closes and again over the next five runs.

## D157 applies
One acceptance criterion per red-green cycle, checked from git (5-card experiment, D157):
- The slice (architect, ctx-2) numbers the criteria 1 to 3 before any red.
- Each red commit body carries "Criterion: n".
- The green for criterion n lands before any red for n+1.
- Greens are pushed at once.
- ZOMBIES already in the card are implemented by QA, not rewritten (a ZOMBIES change is a card-text fix through this window).
- Each commit stays within D136, cites D163 and D164, red first (D137).

## D158 applies
The facilitator's pre-window checklist (D158) is run before this window opens: the proposal names seats for ready, slice, red, green, ship and signoff; the reviewer seat is not named auditor; the roster is not template boilerplate; every seat has a domain/why and a distinct context; the Claude reason cites a probe file and time (01:20 UTC); the card text lines match the proposal (second section below); every declared role is listed for polling (checklist file to be committed before the window, as for windows 208-taskforce, 210-taskforce and 219-taskforce); the repositories (phrase-lang for the card and window, mob-defaults for the code) and the working directory of every command are named.

## D165 applies (Intent line)
Before the first red of each criterion that implements owner direction, the red seat writes "Intent: <what the owner wants and why>" in its record, quoting the owner and naming the D-number. For this card the line quotes D163 (the owner's words: "I just want the rotation to even out and don't just jump to all Claude like has happened in the past"; no new strictness beyond that intent) and D164 (the mechanism: least-recently-used model per seat from a tracked seat-use history, Claude refused only while another available model has waited longer), and says this card applies the same rules to decision seats. The facilitator confirms the line against D163 and D164 (D165 C2); a criterion is "no intent question" only where it is mechanical (for example the recorded model, probe time and reason in the decision record).

## D166 applies (assumption line)
This card changes a rule, so the slice (architect, ctx-2) writes an assumption line before the first red: "Assumption: <what the slice takes as true that could be wrong, and how it is checked>". Candidates the architect should consider: decider.py can reach the facilitator's seat-use history for the repository it votes on (--repo); a Decider run is one card's context, so the card id and the context in a seat-use line name the window or Decider (for example 226-taskforce ctx-n) without a new field; a refusal at the first voter can leave the other voters unlaunched because the check runs before the pool starts. The facilitator confirms the line against the slice.

## Window rule
- Every declared role is polled (F-054): all seven role seats answer (ready ctx-1 is the proposer; slice ctx-2, red ctx-3, green ctx-4, reviewer ctx-5, ship ctx-6, signoff ctx-7), each in its own fresh context. A declared role that is not polled makes the window invalid.
- Each seat answers either "no objection" or ONE fixed condition per objection (D145). A condition that is simply adopted and re-polled stays in the window; an unsettled objection goes to a full Decider.
- Card-text changes proposed with this declaration are card-text fixes in the same window (D153 L1).
- The poll is itself a set of decision seats that card 226 has not yet put under the gate, so the facilitator applies the card's rule by hand and records it in the window: the voters start on a probe under 60 minutes old (re-probe first if the 01:20 UTC probe is 60 minutes old or more at poll time, 02:20 UTC), and each voter's model, probe time and reason are written in the window record.

## Why this is neither a one-way door nor a standing-rule change
Two-way door: the declaration ends with the card (and can be re-declared by another window); nothing is published, deleted or migrated, and the roster can be changed by a Decider mid-card. The code change is reversible too: revert the decider.py commit; no record, seat-use line or D-record changes, and card-mode seats are untouched. It is not a standing-rule change: the rule was decided in D163 (the owner's balanced-rotation intent) and D164 (least-recently-used from a tracked history) and built for card-mode seats by card 208; this card applies the same rule to decision seats and this declaration applies Task-Force Driven Development, D136, D145, D153, D157, D158, D165 and D166 as written, changing no agreement, D-record or checker.
